messages.content: Which substance causes dopamine levels in the brain's reward system to rise by about 25%-40% when administered directly?

A. Heroin
B. Cocaine
C. Barbiturates
D. Nicotine

Correct answer: D
Which diagnostic imaging technique provides a moving image of a body part or organ?

A. X-ray
B. Ultrasound
C. CT scan
D. Fluoroscopy

Correct answer: D
Which tests should both the expectant mother and her partner undergo before trying to conceive to ensure a healthy pregnancy?

A. Cervical smear test and urinalysis for the mother, complete STD tests and AIDS test for the partner.
B. Complete STD tests, AIDS test, and cervical smear test for both the mother and her partner.
C. Rubella vaccination and urinalysis for the mother, complete STD tests and AIDS test for the partner.
D. Cervical smear test and complete blood tests for the mother, complete STD tests, AIDS test, and urinalysis for the partner.

Correct answer: B
Which surgical procedure allows for small incisions, reduces post-operative pain, and minimizes abdominal scarring?

A. Open Appendectomy
B. Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
C. Conventional Hernia Surgery
D. Laparoscopic Hernia Surgery

Correct answer: D
Which diagnostic tests are necessary for the confirmation of Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH) after the identification of an osteolytic lesion on radiography?

A. Only a biopsy is required for confirmation.
B. Computed tomography (CT) is necessary to assess the degree of bone destruction.
C. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is necessary to assess soft tissue infiltration.
D. All of the above.

Correct answer: D
Which laboratory test is valuable for screening disorders related to anemia, infection, blood diseases (like leukemia and lymphoma), and problems with blood clotting?

A. SGOT test
B. SGPT test
C. CBC test
D. Lipid panel

Correct answer: C
What is the difference between an agonist and an inverse agonist in the context of receptors?

A. An agonist is a molecule that binds to a receptor and produces a response, while an inverse agonist is a molecule that binds to a receptor and inhibits the response.
B. An agonist is a molecule that binds to a receptor and blocks the response, while an inverse agonist is a molecule that binds to a receptor and enhances the response.
C. An agonist is a molecule that binds to a receptor and produces a response, while an inverse agonist is a molecule that binds to a different receptor and produces a response.
D. An agonist is a molecule that binds to a receptor and produces a response, while an inverse agonist is a molecule that binds to a different site on the same receptor and inhibits the response.

Correct answer: A
Which disease progresses quickly and significantly in the liver during HIV infection?

A. Hepatitis A
B. Hepatitis C
C. Mycobacterium infection
D. Chronic kidney disease

Correct answer: B
Which text is a comprehensive reference book on the endocrine system?

A. Greenstein, B. & Wood, D. (2011). The Endocrine System at a Glance.
B. Rushton, L. & Cooley, D. A. (2004). The endocrine system.
C. Sharpey-Schafer, E. A. (1926). The endocrine organs: P.
D. None of the above

Correct answer: A
Which condition is associated with an increased risk of undetermined minute haematuria and from time to time overtpapillary necrosis?

A. Chronic severe MR
B. Valvular plane figure disease
C. Diabetes with reap hook attribute
D. Cystic urinary organ diseases

Correct answer: C
Based on the text, which imaging modality is best for evaluating tendon physique and morphology?

A. 1.5T-weighted sequences
B. CT scans
C. MRI with fat suppression
D. X-rays

Correct answer: A
Which of the following factors contributes the most to antibiotic resistance in your country?

A. The use of antibiotics prescribed by physicians based on accurate bacterial diagnoses.
B. The misuse and unnecessary use of antibiotics by patients without consulting a physician.
C. The overuse of antibiotics in livestock farming.
D. The lack of national guidelines and policies for the use of antibiotics.

Correct answer: B
Which biological systems have been consistently demonstrated to be altered in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD)?

A) The neuroendocrine and immune systems
B) The cardiovascular and respiratory systems
C) The musculoskeletal and digestive systems
D) The renal and endocrine systems

Correct answer: A
Which section of the text discusses the properties, functions, and disorders related to the circulatory system?

A. 1.1 Histology and Histological Techniques
B. 2.3 Circulation
C. 2.5 Excretion
D. 2.6 Endocrine Glands

Correct answer: B
Which structures are located in the interstitial space between proximal and distal tubules?

A. Arterioles and venules
B. Interlobular arteries and interlobular veins
C. Peritubular capillaries
D. Interstitial fibrosis and edema

Correct answer: C
Which of the following statements about sleep apnea is not true?

A. Sleep apnea is a condition characterized by an excessively narrow airway.
B. Sleep apnea can lead to serious effects on the body and the mind.
C. There is no cure for sleep apnea.
D. Snoring and sleep apnea are the same thing.

Correct answer: D
What are some benefits of using mouthwash in addition to brushing and flossing?

A. It helps in sealing dentinal tubules in sensitive teeth and relieves pain.
B. It keeps cavities and periodontal disease away by strengthening tooth enamel and preventing dental decay.
C. It kills germs that hurt teeth and gums and stops bacterial growth.
D. It changes the pH of the mouth and deters the production of microorganisms.

Correct answer: C
Who will perform the intra-articular injections of mesenchymal stem cells?

A. The patient themselves
B. A certified clean room facility operated by Magellan Stem Cells
C. A suitably qualified procedural clinician with an MBBS degree
D. An appropriately qualified medical clinician performing liposuction

Correct answer: C
Which type of genes are more likely to be associated with diseases based on their regulatory load?

A. Genes with low regulatory load
B. Genes with medium regulatory load
C. Genes with high regulatory load
D. Genes with no regulatory load

Correct answer: C
Which blood tests are essential before a chemotherapy process?

A. CBC and Blood chemistry tests
B. AST and ALT tests
C. PT and PTT tests
D. INR test

Correct answer: A
What is the diagnosis for the given histology and immunostaining results?

A. Solitary fibrous tumor
B. Lobular capillary hemangioma
C. Sinonasal hemangiopericytoma
D. Glomus tumor

Correct answer: C
What is the primary focus of the study discussed in the text?

A. Generating testable hypotheses about the molecular mechanisms of environmental diseases.
B. Developing a text mining solution to enhance manual curation throughput and efficiency.
C. Exploring the molecular mechanisms of action of environmental chemicals and the genetic basis of differential susceptibility.
D. Classifying compounds with respect to toxicity prediction using focused gene microarrays.

Correct answer: A
Which category of medications does the text mention as having a value CAGR of over 1% from 2013-2018?

A. Antihistamines
B. Antipruritics
C. Antifungals
D. Antiseptics

Correct answer: B
Which species of mosquitoes prefer to breed in salt water marshes?

A. Anopheles quadrimaculatus
B. Culex salinarius
C. Aedes sollicitans
D. Aedes aegypti

Correct answer: A
Based on the text, which of the following is a drug used to treat Parkinson's disease?

A. Hemmings C
B. Aarsland et al.
C. Rivastigmine
D. Galantamine

Correct answer: C
What are some common objects that can be aspirated and what factors influence the location and prognosis of aspirated objects in the respiratory tract?

A. Commonly aspirated objects include seeds, nuts, bone fragments, nails, small toys, coins, pins, medical instrument fragments, dental appliances, and oily nuts. The location and prognosis of aspirated objects depend on the patient's age, physical position during aspiration, and the inflammatory response to the object.
B. Commonly aspirated objects include vegetables, fruits, and liquids. The location and prognosis of aspirated objects depend on the patient's dietary habits and the speed of aspiration.
C. Commonly aspirated objects include water, air, and gases. The location and prognosis of aspirated objects depend on the patient's breathing pattern and lung capacity.
D. Commonly aspirated objects include metals, plastics, and synthetics. The location and prognosis of aspirated objects depend on the patient's occupation and exposure to industrial materials.

Correct answer: A
According to the text, which of the following is a potential indication of diabetes in the mouth?

A. White spots in the mouth
B. Bleeding gums
C. Swollen gums
D. Bad breath

Correct answer: B
What is the goal of the study described in the text?

A. To develop a mathematical model of bone tissue homeostasis in multiple myeloma patients.
B. To understand the role of osteoblasts and osteoclasts in bone tissue redesigning in multiple myeloma.
C. To test the effectiveness of denosumab in inhibiting RANKL and reducing bone resorption in multiple myeloma patients.
D. To investigate the pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of denosumab in multiple myeloma patients.

Correct answer: D
Which phase of CT scan is best for evaluating the wall of the hollow viscera?

A. Arterial phase
B. Portal-venous phase
C. Delayed phase
D. Early arterial phase

Correct answer: B
Which of the following substances can cause liver problems when ingested in large amounts through contaminated water?

A. Copper
B. Norovirus
C. Giardia
D. Hepatitis A

Correct answer: A
A patient is diagnosed with a thyroid nodule. Which of the following is the recommended initial course of action?

A. Repeat FNA or US if nodule persists
B. Close observation with periodic thyroid studies and physical exam
C. Cold surgery
D. Hot surgery

Correct answer: A
Which condition requires prompt medical attention due to the potential danger of an underlying condition and can be diagnosed through history and physical examination?

A. Food-borne illnesses
B. Cardiovascular disease
C. Headaches
D. Shoulder dislocations

Correct answer: C
Which of the following conditions is associated with large, single abscesses located in the incorrectly lobe of the liver and the absence of antineuronal antibodies?

A. Renal disease
B. Paraneoplastic cerebellar degeneration
C. Marrow rate disorders
D. Body substance organic phenomenon

Correct answer: B
Which types of insects can provide useful information to investigators about a deceased body at a crime scene?

A. Mosquitoes and bees
B. Maggots and beetles
C. Ants and termites
D. Butterflies and moths

Correct answer: B
Which areas of the brain have shown perfusion hyperactivity in chronic pain conditions?

A. Prefrontal cortex only.
B. Insular cortex only.
C. Parietal, insular, cingulate, and frontal cortical areas, thalamus, amygdala, and midbrain.
D. Gray matter only.

Correct answer: C
Which condition is associated with symptoms of impaired intestinal absorption, insidious onset, and otalgia?

A. Appendicitis
B. Rubella
C. Meningitis
D. Cholangitis

Correct answer: B
What is the therapeutic index and side effects of Viagra?

A. The therapeutic index of Viagra is 10 and it causes cycloplegia lasting 7-9 days.
B. Viagra has a narrow therapeutic index and its side effects include myoglobinuria and bone marrow toxicity.
C. Viagra has a high therapeutic index and its side effects include hypotension and dermatitis.
D. Viagra is a pure antagonist and its side effects include impotence and loss of faith in the patient.

Correct answer: B
Which of the following statements is true about DAA (Diclofenac Sodium) in the surgical population?

A. It has a high relative incidence of severe operative bleeding.
B. It has a low incidence of black or severe hemorrhage, including intracranial bleed.
C. Its use is not recommended due to the increased risk of severe hemorrhage and metastases.
D. Its use is recommended due to its anti-infective properties for intra-abdominal infections.

Correct answer: B
Which advanced treatment is used for healing wounds by significantly increasing the amount of oxygen in the bloodstream and delivering more oxygen to the wound?

A. Skin grafting
B. Hyperbaric Oxygen Therapy
C. Tissue flaps
D. Epidermal skin grafting

Correct answer: B
Which finding suggests that the acute endogenous fibrinolytic capacity is important in determining future cardiovascular risk?

A. Net t-PA release was 44% lower in patients who experienced atherothrombotic events during follow-up.
B. Intra-brachial infusion of tumour necrosis factor-a impaired NO-dependent vasodilatation and increased basal t-PA concentrations.
C. Sildenafil did not affect endothelium-dependent vasodilatation or acute t-PA release.
D. Genetic variation within the t-PA gene has no effect on t-PA release in patients with CHD.

Correct answer: A
Which bacteria are mentioned in the text as causing symptoms of diarrhea and are transmissible through contaminated water or food?

A. Campylobacter, E. coli, and Salmonella
B. Staphylococcus aureus, Salmonella, and Listeria monocytogenes
C. Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Moraxella catarrhalis
D. Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Staphylococcus saprophyticus

Correct answer: A
Which complication of a paraesophageal hernia repair requires immediate detection and treatment with a barium esophagram?

A. Herniation
B. Gastric/esophageal perforation
C. Nausea and vomiting
D. Pneumothorax

Correct answer: B
According to the text, which local anesthetic agent is superior to body part diazepam in children when intramuscular or intranasal administration is necessary?

A. Midazolam
B. Lidocaine
C. Fentanyl
D. Propofol

Correct answer: A
Based on the text, which condition is associated with a twofold increased risk for cardiovascular events such as myocardial infarction and stroke in women?

A. Meningitis
B. Migraine with aura
C. Ankylosing spondylitis
D. Systemic lupus erythematosus

Correct answer: B
Which group of people are most likely to transmit Cytomegalovirus (CMV) to others?

A. People with a healthy immune system
B. People with immune deficiencies
C. Children under three years old
D. Pregnant women

Correct answer: C
What are the recommendations for survivors to detect melanoma skin cancer early?

A. Request a full-body skin examination during their annual primary health care examinations, perform skin self-exams each month, and use the ABCDE method to check for changes in moles.
B. Avoid using the ABCDE method to check for changes in moles and instead rely solely on regular skin examinations by doctors.
C. Use the ABCDE method to check for changes in freckles and sun spots instead of moles.
D. Avoid performing monthly self-examinations and only rely on free SPOTme® skin cancer screenings.

Correct answer: A
Which ribs are referred to as 'floating' ribs in the body?

A. 1st and 2nd pairs
B. 3rd and 4th pairs
C. 11th and 12th pairs
D. 5th and 6th pairs

Correct answer: C
According to the text, which part of the body is referred to as the 'core of one's health'?

A. Brain
B. Heart
C. GI system
D. Muscles

Correct answer: C
Why is it difficult to study circulating tumor cells, which are a potentially rich source of information about a person's cancer?

A. They are abundant in the blood
B. They are easily accessible through a simple blood test
C. They contain different proteins than the original tumor
D. They are evenly distributed throughout the body

Correct answer: C
Which type of acne scar looks like a series of deep, narrow holes in the skin?

A. Rolling scar
B. Box scar
C. Icepick scar
D. Hypertrophic scar

Correct answer: C
Which of the following symptoms would require a healthcare provider to perform an arthrocentesis procedure to take out fluid from the sore joint?

A. Gradual and mild joint pain that lasts less than 3 days
B. Severe and sudden joint pain on one side
C. Stiffness in the joints that lasts less than 30 minutes in the morning
D. Severe and unexplained joint pain with other unexplained symptoms

Correct answer: D
Which of the following conditions is associated with foot drop and leg pain?

A. Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation
B. Paracetamol overdose
C. Lymphadenopathy
D. Diabetic neuropathy

Correct answer: D

Which course covers the study of the Microbiology including bacterial flora of the conjunctiva and eyelid, bacteria associated with eye disease, basics of ocular cultures and techniques for specimen staining?

A. Introduction to patient care procedures in ophthalmology.
B. Techniques of modern ophthalmic photography.
C. Introduction to patient care procedures in ophthalmology with emphasis on the Microbiology.
D. Ocular motility and A-Scan biometry.

Correct answer: C
Which two professions are identified as critical contributors in addressing antibiotic resistance through infection control, antimicrobial stewardship, and diagnostic stewardship?

A. Dentists and pharmacists
B. Nurses and pharmacists
C. Pharmacists and medical laboratory personnel
D. Physicians and pharmacists

Correct answer: C
Based on the text, which protein is being studied for its role in osteoclast function and bone resorption, and what specific function of the protein is being investigated?

A. Paxillin, role in OC formation
B. RANKL, role in OC activation
C. Osteocalcin, role in bone formation
D. Paxillin, role in OC polarization and adhesion

Correct answer: A
What are the techniques and methods used in this doctoral thesis for analyzing protein expression in situ in cells and tissues using affinity reagents?

A. Developing and implementing techniques for simultaneous purification, concentration, and labeling of antibodies using a novel method on solid phase.
B. Utilizing Affibody molecules as an alternative affinity reagent in bioimaging and immunoassays.
C. Performing systematic analysis of protein expression using antibody-based bioimaging approaches, such as immunofluorescence (IF) and immunohistochemistry (IHC).
D. Applying antibody-based bioimaging proteomics as a platform for biomarker discovery, specifically identifying and studying the candidate biomarker SATB2 for colorectal cancer.

Correct answer: C
Which treatment has shown promising results for a patient with neuroendocrine cancer, according to the experiences shared in the text?

A. Chemotherapy
B. Radiation therapy
C. Afinitor (Everolimus)
D. PRRT (Peptide Receptor Radionuclide Therapy)

Correct answer: C
Which method provides high resolution of the protein structure but does not give information about its conformational flexibility?

A. X-ray crystallography
B. Protein NMR
C. Computational modeling
D. Circular dichroism

Correct answer: A
Based on the text, which ion is secreted into the vasiform limb by an anion exchanger in the top membrane?

A. Hydrogen ion (H+)
B. Chloride ion (Cl-)
C. Bicarbonate ion (HCO3-)
D. Sulfate ion (SO42-)

Correct answer: C
What is the procedure for placing a bridge, including what is reshaped and what is made in a lab?

A. The tooth is reshaped and a temporary crown is placed, while the permanent crown is made in a lab. The permanent crown is then cemented in on a follow-up visit.
B. The teeth on both sides of the space are reshaped and an impression is taken, which is used to make a temporary bridge in the lab. The permanent bridge is then cemented in on a follow-up visit.
C. The tooth is reshaped and an impression is taken, which is used to make a temporary bridge in the lab. The permanent bridge, made of gold, is then cemented in on a follow-up visit.
D. The teeth on both sides of the space are reshaped and an impression is taken. The temporary bridge is made in the office and cemented in place, while the permanent bridge is made in a lab and cemented in on a follow-up visit.

Correct answer: B

Which surgical procedure is used to fix a condition where there is impaired drainage from one or both kidneys, and minimally invasive surgical options offered include robotic pyeloplasty or pure laparoscopic pyeloplasty?

A. Appendectomy
B. Ileostomy
C. Cholecystectomy
D. Pyeloplasty

Correct answer: D
According to the text, what are the four prevention steps recommended by the CDC to help prevent food poisoning at home?

A. Clean, Separate, Cook and Chill.
B. Cook, Chill, Clean and Separate.
C. Separate, Cook, Chill and Clean.
D. Chill, Cook, Separate and Clean.

Correct answer: A
Which factors contribute to the formation of peptic ulcer disease (PUD)?

A. Increased acid secretion and Helicobacter pylori infection.
B. Decreased acid secretion and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use.
C. Increased acid secretion and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) use.
D. Decreased acid secretion and Helicobacter pylori infection.

Correct answer: A
Which of the following conditions is associated with the presence of basilar skull fractures, neck stiffness, torticollis, and difficulty swallowing?

A. Retropharyngeal abscess
B. Hepatitis
C. Varicella and zoster
D. Diabetic ketoacidosis

Correct answer: A
Which of the following is a common trigger for asthma attacks in children?

A. Vaccinations
B. Physical exercise
C. Flu-like illnesses
D. Mold in the home

Correct answer: C
Which research project focuses on discovering genetic variants, biomarkers, and mechanisms of drug toxicity using animal models to ultimately lead to new and better-tolerated therapies?

A. The project on chromatin interactions, epigenomics, and transcriptional response to drug induction.
B. The project on early life physiological and psychosocial stress imprints on the gut microbiome in preterm infants.
C. The project on neuronal synaptic and circuit dysfunction in the autism spectrum disorders.
D. The project using diversity outbred mice to study cardiotoxicity of chemotherapeutic agents.

Correct answer: D
Which condition is associated with enlarged anterior cervical adenopathy, lack of significant hemolysis, and decreased spontaneous movement, periodic breathing or obstructive uropathy?

A. Acute myocardial infarction
B. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia (CAH)
C. Meningitis
D. Thyroid cancer

Correct answer: B

A. Hypertension
B. Hypotension
C. Pulmonary embolism
D. Neurotrophic bedsores

Correct answer: C
Which medication is a competitive antidote for leukotriene receptor antagonists and should be administered in case of overdose?

A. Glucocorticosteroids
B. ACE inhibitors
C. Heparin
D. NSAIDs

Correct answer: A
Which document provides the case definition of neuropathy used in the study?

A. Finnerup et al. 2016
B. Tesfaye et al. 2010
C. The text describing the study procedures
D. Lung cancer resection guidelines

Correct answer: B

A. Salicylate and caffeine
B. Acetaminophen and aspirin
C. P-450 and Phase II conjugation reactions
D. Environmental pollutants and bacterial endotoxins

Which section of the text discusses advances in the neurobiology of aging and pathology?

A. Section 1: Cell differentiation and interplay
B. Section 2: Methodologies
C. Section 3: Getting older and pathology
D. The text does not have sections, it only discusses various subjects

Correct answer: C
Which conditions are associated with an increased risk of kidney damage due to the accumulation of potassium?

A. Diabetes mellitus and polycystic kidney disease.
B. Hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism.
C. Anemia and vitamin C deficiency.
D. Hypertension and Parkinson's disease.

Correct answer: A
Which conditions may demonstrate brain atrophy in the medial temporal regions besides Alzheimer's Disease?

A. FTLD
B. Vascular dementia
C. Hippocampal sclerosis
D. Parkinson's Disease

Correct answer: A
Which eye condition causes vision loss by interfering with the flow or drainage of fluid within the eye, resulting in damage to the optic nerve?

A. Macular Degeneration
B. Glaucoma
C. Retinitis Pigmentosa
D. Diabetic Retinopathy

Which is the most common cause of encysted pleural effusions?

A. Tuberculosis
B. Pyogenic infection
C. Congestive cardiac failure
D. Radiation therapy

Correct answer: A
Which vitamins and minerals are prescribed to support the cell structure in dry macular degeneration?

A. Vitamins A, C, and E, and minerals zinc and copper
B. Vitamins B-6, B-9, and B-12
C. Lutein and zeaxanthin
D. Omega-3 long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids (docosahexaenoic acid/eicosapentaenoic acid)

What role does Id1 protein play in body's fat storage and metabolism?

A. It promotes the production of brown and beige fats, which aid in metabolic well-being and prevent diseases.
B. It deactivates PGC 1alpha, inhibiting thermogenesis and the production of brown fat cells.
C. It regulates multiple cellular functions and distributions, but has no impact on fat storage.
D. It activates the production of healthy beige fat and prevents metabolic stress and weight gain.

Which X-linked disorder is characterized by the deletion of the XK gene, leading to the lack of expression of the Kx antigen and the presence of acanthocytes in peripheral blood smears?

A. McLeod syndrome
B. CGD
C. Sickle cell disease
D. Hemolytic anemia

A. Acupuncture
B. Duragesic (fentanyl transdermal system)
C. Senza spinal cord stimulation system
D. Muscle relaxants

A. Viagra
B. Codeine
C. Propranolol
D. Barbiturates

Correct answer: C
Based on the provided text, how did the baby most likely contract dengue infection?

A. From the mother during childbirth.
B. Through breast milk.
C. From a contaminated environment.
D. From a healthcare worker.

Correct answer: A
Which surgical technique for inguinal hernia repair has the shortest operating time on average?

A. SITAPP (single incision transabdominal preperitoneal)
B. TUMP-LS (transumbilical multiport splenectomy)
C. LVHR (laparoscopic ventral hernia repair)

Based on the text, what is the main advantage of using intraoperative MRI during pituitary adenoma resection?

A. It reduces the risk of complications
B. It allows for a more precise diagnosis
C. It enables the surgeon to confirm complete tumor removal during the procedure

Correct answer: C
Which test is recommended to measure the health of the mucosal barrier in the GI tract?

A. Blood test for IgG, IgM and IgA levels.
B. Stool test for intestinal flora and permeability.
C. Skin prick test for food allergens.
D. X-ray or endoscopy to assess intestinal structure.

Which procedure is Dr. Kevin Pauza developing to repair and re-grow damaged discs without the need for spinal fusion?

A. Injection of stem cells into the disc.
B. Use of growth factors to stimulate disc repair.

A. Bachelor's degree in Medicine and Surgery and a Diploma in Physical Medicine
B. Master's degree in Physical Medicine and a Fellowship from the Australian College of Physical Medicine
C. Doctorate in Physical Medicine and a Fellowship from the Royal Australian College of General Practitioners

A. Diabetes and reduced glomerular filtration rate.
B. Arteriosclerosis and male gender.
C. Hypercoagulable states and methysergide use.
D. Peripheral vascular disease and old age.

Correct answer: C

A. Alveus

C. Cingulum

Based on the text, which organ does the heart abut onto posteriorly?

A. Liver
B. Stomach

B. The patient has a pulmonary arterio-venous fistula (PAVF) caused by a dietary factor bypassing the liver.
